title: Twenty-three local properties of a morphism are insensitive to extending a finite order thickening of the target
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)

difficulty_reason: Given a morphism (f, f') of thickenings over a finite order thickening S in S' with X' flat over S' and the two base-change identities X = S x_{S'} X', Y = S x_{S'} Y', the lemma proves that twenty-three listed properties hold for f exactly when they hold for f'. The proof has two clearly separated halves. The forward direction is a blanket argument: every listed property is stable under base change, so a citation list discharges it at once. The converse is where the work is, and it is done property by property, each step reducing the property of f' to a property of f along the thickening. The load-bearing content is the converse direction together with the finiteness and local-freeness endgame, which uses that f' is proper and that a proper finite-fibre morphism over a thickening is finite, then derives finite local freeness from flatness and finite presentation. Retained author proof at lines 2336-2560.
